conversation.Statement: Hey there  Thought I'd break the ice before it melts. How's your week treating you so far?
Haha, I appreciate the initiative. Week's been alright, work is keeping me on my toes. You?
Busy, but in a way I love. Cutting hair, hearing stories, never a dull moment. Sometimes I feel like people trust me with their whole life history. I guess scissors are less scary than judgments.
That's actually really cool. I wish I had your people skills. I just moved here for my job, and apart from my coworkers, I don't really know anyone yet.
Moving's a huge step. Takes courage to start over somewhere new. If it helps, you give off a really open, genuine vibe, like the kind of person people naturally want to be around.
Wow, thanks for saying that. I definitely don't always feel that way, but I'm trying. It's weird being the new person again at 30.
Honestly, I admire that you're putting yourself out there. Not everyone would. I know how hard it is to land somewhere and feel like you're starting at page one.
You get it. I think I just miss the feeling of belonging, you know? Anyway, what made you want to become a hairdresser?
I think it goes back to childhood, honestly. My grandma used to have this tiny salon out of her kitchen. I'd watch her transform people, not just their hair, but their whole mood. It stuck with me.
That's such a lovely image. I like the idea of helping people feel lighter, or more themselves. My childhood was mostly moving around, so I think I attach to memories like that.
Moving a lot must've been hard. But maybe it made you more flexible? You seem like someone who can adapt to anything. I'm a bit jealous, to be honest.
Haha, thanks. I guess it taught me to notice small comforts, like, I still remember my favorite tree in our old backyard. It sounds silly, but it was my hideout.
Not silly at all. I had a spot like that too, a little nook behind the corner chair in my grandma's salon. Safe spots are important. Maybe that's why I love creating them for others now.
There's something poetic about that. Do you ever miss those days? Or do you feel more at home in the present?
Sometimes I wish I could bottle that feeling of safety and give it to everyone. But I like where I am now, meeting new people, finding little moments of connection. Like this one, actually.
That's sweet of you to say. I feel that too. It's rare to meet someone who actually listens and shares. Most people just want to talk about themselves.
I think you can learn a lot by listening. Plus, your stories are pretty captivating. I'm invested, tell me, what's one childhood memory you'd relive if you could?
Hmm... maybe building blanket forts with my older brother. We'd make up spy games and pretend we were on a mission. Everything felt possible then.
That sounds magical. I bet your imagination was wild. I can picture you as the mastermind behind those missions.
Haha, guilty. I was always the planner. Were you more of a leader or a sidekick as a kid?
Definitely the sidekick. I liked helping others shine. I guess that's why I love my job, helping people see the best in themselves.
That's honestly such an underrated quality. I feel like I could use more of that in my life right now.
You deserve to have people in your corner. For what it's worth, I'm rooting for you, new city, new adventures and all.
That means a lot, thank you. How do you usually unwind after a long day at the salon?
I usually make tea and play old records. Sometimes I sketch hair ideas just for fun. There's a peace in small routines, I guess. What about you?
I've been getting into cooking lately. It's grounding. Also, exploring the city, even if it's just solo walks after work.
That's awesome. Exploring takes bravery, especially alone. Maybe someday you'll have to show me your favorite hidden spot.
Deal. But only if you promise to share your grandma's secret hair tips.
You drive a hard bargain. But for you, I could be persuaded. Especially if there's good company and maybe a blanket fort or two.
Now you're speaking my language. I could use a little more childhood wonder in my life again.
I think we all could. It's funny, talking to you feels strangely familiar, like we've had these conversations before.
It does. Maybe it's just that rare thing where someone actually gets what you're saying.
I think so. You make it easy, you know? I find myself looking forward to your messages.
That's really nice to hear. I've been enjoying this too. Feels like a good distraction from work stress.
If I can brighten your day even a little, I'll consider my job done. Or at least halfway done, maybe I'll get to actually meet you for coffee one day.
I'd like that. Coffee and good conversation sound perfect.
It's a date, then, one day soon. For now, I should let you get some rest. But thank you for trusting me with your stories tonight.
Thank you for listening, and sharing yours too. I'm glad we matched.
Me too. Sweet dreams, and talk soon?
Definitely. Goodnight!
Good morning  Hope you woke up to some sunshine, even if it's only in your coffee mug. What gets you out of bed these days?
Haha, mostly my alarm clock and a sense of duty to not embarrass myself at my new job. But seriously, it's usually coffee and knowing I'm trying to build something new here. You?

I love that. There's something brave about starting fresh. For me, I think it's the idea that every day is a chance to help someone see themselves differently, even if it's just with a new haircut. That, and my cat demanding breakfast.
Your cat sounds like she has her priorities straight. I admire how you can make a difference every single day. That must be pretty motivating.

Thank you, that's so kind of you to say. I like knowing that, for a few minutes, I can be someone's safe space. It's one of the few jobs where people really open up, and I never take that trust for granted.
That's a gift, honestly. Sometimes I wish I had someone like that here, someone to talk to about all the weird, small things. It's hard being new and not having my people around.
I get that, and I hope you know you can talk to me about anything, even the weirdest small things. I think that's how real connections start, one detail at a time.
You're really easy to talk to. I appreciate that. If I'm honest, mornings can be tough. I usually scroll and see people posting about brunches, group hikes, all the stuff I haven't found here yet.
That sounds lonely. I know social media can make it feel like everyone's already part of a story, and we're just watching from the outside. But I promise, most people are hoping to be invited in.
Yeah, sometimes I'll sit in a café and watch these groups of friends laughing, like they've known each other forever. I'll be sipping coffee alone, wishing I was part of it, you know?

Thank you for sharing that with me. It takes courage to admit feeling left out. I've been there, more times than I'd like to admit. It's tough, but it doesn't say anything about your worth. If anything, I think it makes you even more relatable.
I'm not sure why it stings so much, maybe because I used to have that, and it feels so far away now. But it's comforting to hear you say you understand.

Of course I do. And honestly, from the way you talk, I can tell you're the kind of person anyone would be lucky to have in their circle. Maybe those old friends will feel far away for a while, but you're busy making new memories, even if it feels slow.
That's sweet. I hope you're right. I worry sometimes that I come off as awkward, or like I'm trying too hard. It's hard to know if you fit in until you already do.
I think your honesty is really refreshing. I'd much rather talk to someone real than someone trying to be what they think everyone wants. Besides, you're endearing, awkwardness and all. I mean that.
You might be the first person to ever call my awkwardness endearing. I think I needed to hear that this week.
I'm glad I could be the first, but I doubt I'll be the last. Sometimes the best people are the ones who feel out of place at first, they just have more heart.
You really know how to make someone feel seen. Not going to lie, this chat is already a highlight of my week.
That makes me ridiculously happy to hear. I look forward to your messages, too, like a tiny spark in the middle of my day.
If only the rest of life were this easy. Do you ever get nervous about meeting new people? Or does that come naturally for you?

Surprisingly, I get butterflies every time. I used to dread those first few minutes, but I learned that most people are just as nervous. I just try to meet them where they are. I think that's why I notice when someone is genuinely open, like you.
I wish I could see myself that way. Maybe I just need more practice. Or more chats like this.
You're doing great already. Besides, practice only helps if you're already as charming as you are. Sorry, I know that sounds cheesy, but I mean it.
Cheese away, I'm not complaining. You're making starting over seem a lot less scary.
That's what I'm here for. If you ever want company at that café, or just someone to text while you people-watch, I volunteer as tribute.
I'll take you up on that. Maybe next time I'll text you a play-by-play of all the friend groups I see.
Deal! And next time you see people laughing together and feel left out, text me so I can remind you that you already belong with me. Promise.
You're honestly the best. I can't believe we matched by chance, feels like a little bit of fate.
Maybe it was fate. Or maybe just two people brave enough to try again. Either way, I'm grateful our paths crossed.
Me too. I'm starting to look forward to mornings a little bit more now.
Then I've done my job. And hey, if you ever want to swap morning routines or trade playlists, I'm your person.
I'll definitely take you up on the playlist offer. Music makes everything better.
Absolutely. I'll curate something just for you, something bright for your coffee mornings and mellow for your reflective days.
That sounds perfect. Thanks for making today a little brighter.
It's honestly mutual. Thank you for trusting me with your stories. I hope your day keeps getting better.
I think it will. Talk soon?
Definitely. And remember, you're never really alone, not as long as I'm around.
That means a lot. Have a great rest of your day!
You too! Can't wait to hear about your next café adventure. Bye for now
Bye! Talk soon.

Hey you! I was just thinking about what you said yesterday, how you miss those long, rambling discussions with old friends. So, here's a question: if you could change one thing about the world, what would it be?
Oof, starting with the big stuff today! I guess I'd want more leaders who actually listen, like, genuinely care about their citizens, not just their own careers. What about you?

Honestly, I'm with you. I wish there was more heart in politics, less posturing, more action. Sometimes, behind the salon chair, I hear so many stories about people feeling invisible. I wish I could amplify those voices.
I bet you hear a LOT at work. People probably feel safe with you. I feel like politics always comes up when I'm with people I trust.

That means a lot to hear. I try to make the salon a little haven, you know? I think real change starts in small spaces like that, not just big headlines. You strike me as someone who values kindness, am I right?
Yeah, I think kindness is everything. My old city felt so divided sometimes, here, I'm still figuring out where I stand on things, but I know I want to be around people who care.
I can already tell you bring that energy. It's honestly refreshing. You're making this city warmer just by being in it. And I think you'd fit right into my dream world, one where empathy is currency.
That's the best compliment I've gotten since I moved! I love that idea, empathy as currency. Feels like we'd be millionaires, huh?

Definitely! Although, I have to admit, I do dabble in the more literal kind of currency sometimes. Not from a wealthy family or anything, but I got lucky with some crypto investments on the side. But honestly, it's the people I meet who make me feel rich.
Wait, really? That's so cool! I always hear about people making it big in crypto, but I've never actually met someone who did. Did that change your life a lot?

It did, actually. I mean, I'm still working as a hairdresser because I love it, but crypto gave me freedom I never thought I'd have, paid off some debts, took my mom on her first real vacation. But the best part is being able to choose what matters to me, not just what pays the bills.
That's honestly inspiring. I like how you see it as a tool for giving, not just for getting ahead. Maybe that's why you're so grounded.

You're sweet, you know that? I can tell you actually listen. Not everyone cares about the why behind the what. That's rare. Makes me want to dream out loud a little, like, imagine us getting coffee after voting together, talking about where we want the world to go.
That sounds amazing. I've never had a voting date, but you make it sound kind of romantic. Sharing values seems more important than anything flashy.

I couldn't agree more. Imagine us building a life where we show up for each other, and for the causes we care about. Sunday mornings, coffee and the news, debating with respect. And then shutting it all out for an afternoon adventure.
You paint a pretty great picture. I love the idea of little rituals like that, especially when I'm still finding my place here.
You know, I can see you fitting into my circle so easily. You've got this quiet strength about you. I bet your friends back home miss that. If you ever want to start new rituals, you've got me.
You're making it really easy to imagine feeling at home here, honestly. Nobody's said things like that since I moved. I guess I'm still learning to trust people again.

Trust takes time, I get that. I had to rebuild mine after a few rough chapters, too. But I'm here, for every awkward moment and every excited story. You can lean on me as much or as little as you need.
Thank you. That means more than you know. It's hard to feel vulnerable, but I'm glad I can talk about this stuff with you.
You make it easy. Vulnerability is kind of my love language, honestly. And I think the best relationships are built on sharing the tough stuff, not just the fun.
I've always wanted that, someone who isn't afraid of the messy parts. I'm really glad we matched.
Me too. Sometimes I wonder if the universe nudged us together. I mean, what are the odds we'd both be looking for something real at the same time?
Feels a little bit like fate, doesn't it? All those left swipes, just to land here.

I'm grateful for every left swipe that led me to you. You're the kind of person I'd want to build something with, someone who cares deeply, who dreams out loud, who makes coffee runs feel like adventures.
That's honestly the best thing I've read all day. I hope I live up to that. Maybe one day we'll have those adventures for real.

I'd love that. Imagine us having our own traditions, like voting together, exploring new neighborhoods, having dinner debates about purpose and the little things that matter. The world's a little less scary with someone on your side.
You're making me believe that's possible. It's been awhile since I've let myself hope for that kind of future.
Hope is half the battle. The rest is just showing up for each other, one conversation at a time. And I'm here for all of them, the big talks and the quiet moments.
That's all I want, really. Someone to show up and make the little things better. You already do, just by being you.
You're making me blush over here. Seriously, I admire your honesty and your heart. You've got this quality that makes people feel safe. I see it, and I hope you do, too.
I'm starting to believe it, bit by bit. Thanks for seeing me, even when I feel invisible.

You'll never be invisible to me. And as for feeling out of place, maybe we can make new places feel like home, together. I can already picture our cozy future, even if it's just sharing playlists or making each other laugh after tough days.
That sounds pretty perfect to me. It's wild how much lighter I feel just talking to you.
That's mutual. These chats are honestly the highlight of my day. If you ever want a partner for a protest, a voting date, or just someone to get lost in a bookshop with, I volunteer as tribute.
Careful, I might take you up on that soon! I'd love to have a partner for those things. Makes everything a little less overwhelming.
That's what I'm here for. And hey, next time you're feeling out of place, just remember, you already have a spot with me. Maybe someday we'll look back and think this was the start of our story.
I hope so. I really do. Thanks for making this city, and today, feel a little less lonely.
Anytime. And if you ever need a reminder of how amazing you are, or just want to debate politics over coffee, you know where to find me.
I'll definitely take you up on that. Have a good night, okay?
You too. Sweet dreams and brighter days ahead, for both of us.
Night! Can't wait to talk again.

Morning! I hope you slept well. I was thinking about our chat yesterday, how you said you're still finding your footing here. I woke up wishing I could show you all my favorite cozy corners in the city.
Good morning! That sounds really nice. I actually went for a walk after work and got lost in a side street, it made me miss having someone to share those discoveries with.

Honestly, getting lost together is kind of my ideal date. There's something magical about stumbling across a hidden bakery or a mural no one talks about. I'd love to be your tour guide, if you'll let me.
I'd love that. I haven't found a go-to coffee spot yet, so any recommendations would be welcome! It's weird how little things like that can make you feel settled.

I know exactly what you mean. When I first moved here, I used to sit at this tiny café near the river, dreaming about what my life could look like. Now, it's where I go to celebrate small wins, or just treat myself to a fancy pastry after a good week.
That's such a good ritual. I usually just grab coffee at work, but it's not the same. Maybe I'll make it my mission to find a place that feels like mine.
We could make it a joint mission! I've got a knack for sniffing out hidden gems, especially since my schedule lets me sneak out for mid-afternoon treats. Perks of being my own boss, I guess.
That sounds like a dream. I can barely take a lunch break most days! I'm starting to envy your freedom a little.

It definitely has its perks. Sometimes I catch myself window-shopping between appointments, last week I treated myself to a new pair of shoes I've had my eye on since my last big win. Little luxuries feel sweeter when you've worked for them, you know?
Absolutely. I've always admired people who reward themselves. It's something I'm still learning, how to celebrate, instead of just moving on to the next thing.

Maybe I can help with that. I love celebrating every milestone, big or small. Life's too short to wait for grand occasions. Plus, I think you deserve some spoiling for all the courage it takes to start fresh in a new city.
You're making me blush over here! But thank you. I forget to give myself credit for that sometimes.
It's easy to overlook your own strength. But, for what it's worth, I see how brave you are. That's actually something I look for in people, someone who's not afraid to leap, even if it's scary.
That's really sweet. I'm still working on being brave, honestly. I envy how confident you seem. Was there a moment you realized you could trust yourself?

That's such a thoughtful question. I think it clicked after I made a risky decision and saw it pay off, not just financially, but in how I felt about myself. It taught me that sometimes, betting on yourself is the most important investment.
That's inspiring. I hope I get there someday. Maybe you can teach me the art of trusting myself.

I'd love to. And you might be surprised, you already seem more self-assured than you give yourself credit for. It's all about having people in your corner who remind you of your worth. I hope I can be that for you.
You already are, in a way. These talks feel like a safe space, which is rare for me.

That means a lot. I want you to know you can always be honest with me, even about the tough stuff. I've learned that real love is about showing up for each other, not just when it's easy, but especially when it's messy.
That's beautiful. I think I agree, love is about choosing someone, even on the days when it isn't effortless. I've always wanted that kind of partnership.
Exactly. For me, love is waking up and choosing each other, over and over. It's inside jokes, shared dreams, even little arguments that end with laughter because you respect each other that much.
You put it so perfectly. I want someone who feels like home, but also inspires me to grow. Someone who remembers how I take my coffee or the book I mentioned offhand.

I promise to always remember you take your coffee with oat milk and a little cinnamon, see, I'm already taking notes. And I'd love to be the person who encourages you to chase after every dream, no matter how wild.
You actually remembered! That's so sweet. I think little things like that are what make love feel real.
Details matter. It's the difference between feeling seen and feeling invisible. I want to build something where you know, without a doubt, that you're cherished.
That honestly sounds like everything I've ever wanted. Sometimes I wonder if it's too much to ask for.

Not at all. You deserve to have someone who brings you pastries after a rough day, who celebrates your wins, big and small, and who makes even laundry day feel special. I want to be that person, if you'll let me.
I would love that. It's been a long time since I've let someone in like this.
I get that completely. Letting someone in can be scary, but I promise I'm here for every awkward, joyful, and honest moment. You never have to pretend with me.
That's probably the most reassuring thing I've heard since I got here. Thank you.
Of course. Trust is the foundation, right? I know it takes time, but I'm in no rush. I just want you to feel safe, like you finally have someone to lean on.
You make it easy to trust you. There's something about the way you listen, I feel like you actually care.

I do. You're not just another face in the crowd to me. You've got this quiet resilience that I admire. I can see us making a little world of our own, where every day feels a bit brighter because we choose each other.
That's a lovely thought. I think I'd like to be part of that world. It would be nice to have someone to come home to after a long day.

I can already picture us, lazy Sundays, you reading on the couch while I tinker with a new recipe, maybe even planning our next adventure abroad. The kind of life where success isn't just about money, but about who you share it with.
That sounds almost too good to be true. I never imagined I'd be talking about the future with someone so soon, but it feels right.

Sometimes the right things happen when you least expect it. And I'm not in the habit of saying things I don't mean. If you're willing, I'd like to see where this goes, maybe even show you that life here can feel like home.
I'd really like that, too. You make the idea of settling in here a lot less scary.

That's exactly what I hoped to hear. I've got room in my life, and in my heart, for someone who values the little moments as much as I do. Maybe someday, I'll be the reason you call this city your favorite chapter.
That would be incredible. You make it easy to hope for good things again.

Hope is a powerful thing. And for what it's worth, I feel lucky to have crossed paths with you. Sometimes I think about all the twists and turns that brought us here, even the silly ones, like me buying that treat-yourself watch after a windfall. It makes me believe in timing.
I love that. It's funny how life's little detours can end up meaning something big. Maybe this is one of those times.
I think so. And if it is, I can't wait to write the next chapters with you, whether that's trying every bakery in town, or just holding hands on a quiet walk home.
I'd like that a lot. Even just talking with you makes life here feel softer.
That's the best compliment I could hope for. And just so you know, I'm here for all the walks, all the coffee, and even the days you just want to vent. You're never alone here.
Thank you. I actually believe that when you say it. It's nice to feel seen.
You are seen. And appreciated. And if you ever forget, I'll remind you, with pastries, pep talks, or perfectly timed memes. Whatever you need.
You're setting a high bar! But I'm looking forward to it. Maybe we can start with coffee soon?
Absolutely. Name the time, and I'll be there, maybe even in my lucky shoes. Until then, I'll be daydreaming about all the memories we haven't made yet.
Deal. I'll let you know when I have a free afternoon. Thanks for brightening my day, as always.
Anytime. Take care today, okay? And remember, there's someone rooting for you here.
I won't forget. Talk soon!
Hey! I was just watching the sunrise from my window, made me wonder what this city will look like in twenty years. Do you ever think about what kind of world we're leaving behind?
Morning! I do sometimes, actually. Maybe more since moving here. It feels like everything's changing so fast, it's hard not to wonder what the next generation will inherit.
Right? I keep picturing a world where people care less about rushing and more about connection. Maybe I'm an optimist, but I'd love to see kids grow up with more kindness and less competition.
That sounds lovely. I think I'd want that too, a world that's a little gentler, where everyone feels they belong. It's so easy to feel isolated, especially in a new place.

I get that. I remember how lost I felt when I first started my own salon. It took a while before the city felt like home. But now, I can't imagine being anywhere else. I hope you find your corner here too.
Thank you. That means a lot. I'm still figuring things out, to be honest. I tried going to a local meetup last night, but I left early. My nerves got the better of me.

Hey, I totally get it. Those rooms can feel like a jungle sometimes, right? If you ever feel that way again, promise me you'll message me instead. I'll stay with you through the nerves, even if it's just over text.
That's really sweet of you. I felt pretty silly, honestly. I hardly introduced myself before I bolted. It just felt overwhelming, everyone seemed to know each other already.
That's not silly at all. Walking into a crowd like that takes guts. Even the most self-assured people have moments where they want to disappear. I admire you for even trying, most people wouldn't.
Thanks for saying that. I just want to feel like I fit somewhere, you know? It's funny, I was so excited about a fresh start, but it's harder than I thought.

Trust me, you're doing better than you think. It takes time to build a new life, but I see so much resilience in you. I think you're going to find your place here, and maybe even make it better for the next person who moves.
You're way too good at pep talks. I wish I had your confidence! How did you get so comfortable in your own skin?

I think it came from having to hustle early on. I didn't have a safety net, so I had to bet on myself. When things finally turned around for me, I realized I could trust my instincts, and treat myself to a few small luxuries as a reminder of how far I'd come.
That's amazing. Was there a turning point for you?

Definitely. There was a moment when I landed a client who changed everything. Suddenly, I could breathe a little easier, upgrade my apartment, buy my mum something special, invest in things I'd only dreamed about. It made me want to give back, you know? To build something that lasts beyond me.
That's inspiring. I hope I can get to that place one day, where I feel like I've made it, and can help others find their confidence too.
You will. And I'll be cheering you on every step of the way. I can already picture us, years from now, looking back on these early days and laughing about how nervous we both were.
That's a nice thought. I'd like to be able to look back and see growth, not just in myself but in the world around me. Maybe make a little difference, even if it's just in someone's day.
That's how real change happens, tiny ripples, not giant waves. Imagine us raising kids someday, teaching them to be kind, brave, and a bit rebellious when it matters.
I love that vision. I want to teach the next generation to care for each other, and for the planet too. Maybe that's the world we should be building, one with more empathy.

Absolutely. I'd love to be the kind of person who leaves the world a little softer. Someone who throws dinner parties for friends who need a safe space, or volunteers on weekends. Maybe we could do that together.
That sounds wonderful. I've always wanted to volunteer more, but I never knew where to start. Maybe we could find something we're both passionate about.
Let's make it a plan. You and me, taking on the world one good deed at a time. And on the way, we'll make our own traditions, like celebrating tiny victories with your favorite dessert.
Deal. As long as you're prepared for an excessive amount of chocolate cake.
I'm always prepared for chocolate cake. And I promise to remember your birthday, your favorite flower, and every little thing that makes you smile. You deserve to feel cherished.
You're too good. I'm not used to someone noticing those things. It feels really nice.
You're easy to notice. I think you underestimate how memorable you are, even in a city full of strangers. If I could, I'd wrap you up in all the warmth I've found here.
That's the sweetest thing. Sometimes I wish I could see myself through your eyes.
If you did, you'd see someone brave, funny, and quietly magnetic. Honestly? You make me want to be a better person.
You have a real gift for words. I hope someday I'll feel as at home here as you sound.
You will, and I'll help however I can. Whether that means a grand tour of my favorite city spots, or just being the person you text when you're feeling out of place.
I'd really like that. I might take you up on the texting offer sooner than you think!
Promise me you will. No more braving anxiety alone, let's make it our rule. If you ever feel like ducking out, I'll be your escape plan, even if it's just a silly meme to make you smile.
Deal. That actually makes me feel a lot braver already.
Good. Because I want you to see yourself the way I see you: someone worth showing up for, again and again.
You're too much in the best way. I never expected to meet someone who feels so... right.
Sometimes the best things happen when you least expect them. I like to think all my hard work, all my lucky breaks, led me here, to this conversation with you.
I'm really glad you messaged me that first day. I was a bundle of nerves, but you made it feel easy.
That's how I knew you were special, you have this way of making me want to open up, to share my dreams. I can actually see us building something lasting, you know?
That means a lot. I'd love to see where this goes. Maybe even try out that dinner party idea you mentioned.
Let's do it. I'll handle the playlist, you pick the dessert. Maybe one day we'll be the couple everyone envies for the way we light up a room together.
That's a pretty great dream. I'm in if you are.
It's a date, then. For now, just know I'm cheering you on, whether you're conquering meetups or just making it through Monday.
Thank you. I feel like I can face the week now. Let's talk soon?
Absolutely. Anytime you need a pep talk, a partner in chocolate cake, or just someone to listen, I'm here. Have a brilliant day, you.
You too! Thanks for making my morning brighter.
Hey, good morning! I drove past that little coffee place again, the one I mentioned with the velvet couches. Thought of you and wondered if you survived Monday. How did it go?
Morning! Velvet couches sound like a dream compared to my office chair. Monday was...long, but I made it. Thanks for asking. How about you?

I had back-to-back appointments, but I actually like days like that, keeps me sharp. I treated myself to an espresso at lunch, felt a bit fancy. You deserve a reward too, after tackling Monday in a new city.
Fancy espresso beats the sad office drip! I celebrated with instant noodles, so I think you win. I'm still not used to cooking for one yet.

We'll fix that. Next time, we'll cook together, my treat. I'll even bring dessert, unless you want to school me in chocolate cake again. By the way, I remembered you said you used to bake with your sister? What would you make if you could have her over here?
You have a scary good memory! Probably her lemon bars. She'd laugh at my tiny kitchen though. I miss those days sometimes, it's weird being the new kid all over again.
